text:
sasha: Heads-up — I'm drafting the Q3 Private Deploy roadmap slice. Focus areas: VPC installer UX, minor/major upgrade paths, and customer-managed routing docs. Need alignment on launch criteria and what we consider 'minimal viable' for field customers.

matt: +1. Key ask from sales: zero-downtime for minor patches, predictable rollback for majors. Also pricing variant for reserved vs self-managed.

julio: Field note: 3 customers specifically asked for BGP peering templates and an IP-preservation option when we upgrade. They run on-prem across heterogeneous NAT boxes.

kai: Proposed acceptance criteria draft: 1) Minor patch (semver patch) supports hotpatch with <=1% request loss in canary; 2) Rollback for minor/major <= 5m to previous operator; 3) Installer supports explicit egress relay for NATed tenants; 4) KMS-backed key rotation demo.

netops: For customer-managed routing we'll need a canonical BGP sample + IP retention policy. Also require a "relay-proxy" fallback for customers who refuse direct peering. That relay has to respect customer egress IPs.

matt: On upgrade path: we should decide between hotpatch (binary-level delta apply) vs operator-restart bundle. Hotpatch reduces downtime but increases complexity and test surface.

sasha: @matt can you sketch the risk table? Hotpatch risks: kernel-level incompat, kv-cache mismatch between versions, requirement for more invariant checks. Benefits: lower SLO impact.

matt: I'll prototype hotpatch daemon and a version-check handshake. Example CLI I plan to use for testing:

```
redwood-operator upgrade --mode hotpatch --timeout 300 --canary 0.05
```

This will stage to 5% traffic, validate KV cache integrity, then roll forward.

julio: Important: add a patchback compatibility test — ensure older clients can still use embeddings endpoint when operator binary changes layout.

netops: Also: document the customer-managed NAT relay config. Minimal fields: `relay_host`, `allowed_prefixes`, `bgp_asn`, `peer_ip`.

sasha: Decision proposal: use hotpatch for patch-level changes (semver patch), operator-restart bundles for minor/major feature sets. Add an opt-in `force-restart` flag for customers who prefer deterministic network state.

kai: Launch gates to agree on: 1) acceptance tests green on two cloud providers + onprem runner; 2) field beta with 3 customers for 6 weeks; 3) runbook + rollback playbook documented; 4) pricing/SLAs scoped for Dedicated vs Private.

deploy-bot: Staging: operator-v1.4.2-hotpatch passed e2e smoke on aws-us-east-1 at 2024-07-24T15:12:03Z. Logs: /staging/builds/4071

matt: Nice — can we capture the KV-corr-check logs for the smoke? Add `kv-checksum` output.

deploy-bot: Attached: `kv-checksum: ok`, `canary-requests: 1200`, `errors: 3 (timed out)`.

julio: Action items: 1) sasha to produce scope doc by EOD Friday with acceptance criteria and SLA columns; 2) matt to deliver hotpatch prototype and basic integration test next Wed; 3) netops to draft BGP/relay template by Tue.

sasha: I'll include a 'patchwork' compatibility matrix in the scope doc to avoid surprises (mapping operator versions -> client SDK compat).

netops: FYI — for relay we need legal signoff on egress IP handling. I'll flag with security/compliance.

kai: Costing note: if customers use relay-proxy for >50% traffic we should treat it as an add-on (egress throughput + HA). Need a clear pricing bucket.

matt: One open question: do we require customers to opt into hotpatch, or is it default for patch updates? My vote: opt-out default (i.e., hotpatch enabled unless customer disables). Safer to default to low disruption.

sasha: Agree default enable, but show explicit consent in installer UI and record opt-out in audit logs.

julio: Quick UX ask: installer should show 'upgrade safety level' (Hotpatch / Bundle restart) with tooltip explaining tradeoffs.

kai: Final check — timeline: prototype + staging tests = 3 weeks; field beta start = Q3 week 5; GA = end of Q3 if beta goes well. Anything blocking that timeline?

matt: Main blocker: hotpatch prototype stability. If prototype slips, fallback plan is to bundle minor patches as blue/green restarts.

sasha: Sounds good. I'll circulate a one-pager with acceptance criteria + decision record after this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:

netops: @sasha please cc me on the one-pager so I can start the BGP template. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Reminder: weekly release sync in #eng-releases tomorrow 10:00.

sasha: Noted — we'll sync progress there and lock decisions on Friday.

matt: I'll add integration tests to CI that validate `kv-checksum` across versions.

julio: Leaving a note for customer success: prepare mention in beta comms about "downtime expectation: near-zero for patch releases, short window for majors".

sasha: Thread summary: hotpatch-by-default for patch releases, bundle-restart for major/minor features, relay-proxy as fallback for NATed customers, BGP + IP-preservation templates required, acceptance criteria + GA gates outlined. Action items assigned.

matt: Awesome. :rocket:
